title: Fix .env Loading in Spring Boot Backend

stories.title: Investigate the root cause of .env not loading
stories.description: As a developer, I need to understand exactly why spring.config.import=optional:file:../.env[.properties] does not load the .env file so I can apply the correct fix.
acceptanceCriteria: Determine the working directory Spring Boot uses when resolving relative paths in spring.config.import
Confirm whether the .env file path (../.env) resolves correctly given that path
Check if the .env file format (KEY=VALUE) is compatible with the [.properties] extension hint
Document the root cause with a comment or in a commit message before proceeding to the fix

stories.title: Fix the .env file loading
stories.description: As a developer, I want the Spring Boot app to correctly load ADMIN_USERNAME, ADMIN_PASSWORD, and JWT_SECRET from the .env file so that admin credentials can be configured without hardcoding.
acceptanceCriteria: Fix the spring.config.import path so .env is found at backend-java/portfolio/.env when running mvn spring-boot:run from that directory
After the fix, AuthService startup log shows the username from .env, not the default admin
JWT_SECRET and ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env are also resolved (not falling back to defaults)
The fix does not break running the app without a .env file (optional: prefix must be preserved)

stories.title: Add a startup warning when credentials fall back to defaults
stories.description: As a developer, I want the app to log a visible warning at startup when ADMIN_USERNAME or ADMIN_PASSWORD resolve to their default values so I immediately know .env is missing or not loaded.
acceptanceCriteria: AuthService @PostConstruct logs a WARN-level message when adminUsername equals 'admin' (the default)
Warning message clearly states that default credentials are in use and recommends setting env vars
No warning is logged when real credentials are loaded from .env
Remove the existing System.out.println debug statements from AuthService.login()

stories.title: Verify the end-to-end login flow with real credentials
stories.description: As a developer, I want to confirm that logging in with the credentials from .env succeeds so I know the fix is complete.
acceptanceCriteria: Start the backend with a .env containing non-default ADMIN_USERNAME and ADMIN_PASSWORD
POST /api/auth/login with those credentials returns a 200 with a JWT token
POST /api/auth/login with admin/admin (the old defaults) returns 401 (confirming defaults are no longer active)
Existing AuthControllerTest tests still pass (mvn test)
